message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a tenant in Texas. (This is general information and not legal advice; for specific situations you may want to consult an attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.) | Area | What the law says | Practical Tips | |------|-------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit and two months for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be returned within 30 days after you move out, minus any lawful deductions (e.g., unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear). | • Get a written receipt and keep a copy of the lease.
• Take photos of the unit before moving in and after moving out. | | **Habitability** | • Texas law requires landlords to maintain the premises in a safe, sanitary condition.
• Repairs for health and safety issues must be made promptly. | • Report problems in writing (email or letter) and keep a copy.
• If the landlord fails to act, you may withhold rent or repair and deduct, but do so only after following the proper procedure. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them and they are reasonable. | • Keep records of all payments.
• If you’re late, communicate with your landlord to avoid disputes. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party can terminate a month‑to‑month lease with 30 days’ written notice.
• For fixed‑term leases, the landlord must give notice if they intend to terminate early. | • Provide written notice (email or letter) and keep a copy. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlords must follow the Texas Property Code’s eviction procedure: serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for non‑payment), file a lawsuit, and obtain a court order.
• Eviction cannot be carried out without a court order. | • If you receive a notice, respond promptly.
• Attend any court hearings and bring documentation. | | **Privacy** | • Landlords may enter the premises only for repairs, inspections, or to show the unit, and must give reasonable notice (usually 24 hours). | • Keep a log of any entries. | | **Discrimination** | • Texas law (and federal Fair Housing Act) prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or other protected classes. | • Report any discriminatory actions to the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major issue, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, but you must follow the correct procedure and keep receipts. | • Document the issue, send a written notice, and keep all receipts. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas does not have statewide rent control; rent increases are governed by the lease agreement. | • Review your lease for any rent‑increase clauses. | | **Utilities** | • The lease should specify which utilities you are responsible for. | • Verify utility responsibilities before signing. | | **Subletting** | • Subletting is allowed only if the lease permits it or the landlord consents. | • Get written permission before subletting. | | **Landlord’s Right to Inspect** | • Landlords can inspect the unit with reasonable notice, but not for harassment or to harass tenants. | • Know your rights to privacy and reasonable notice. | ### Quick Checklist for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Understand rent amount, due date, security deposit limits, pet policies, and notice requirements. 2. **Document Everything** – Photos, videos, written notices, and receipts help protect you in disputes. 3. **Know the Notice Periods** – 30 days for month‑to‑month termination, 24‑hour notice for entry, etc. 4. **Respond Promptly to Notices** – Whether it’s a repair notice or an eviction notice, timely communication can prevent escalation. 5. **Seek Legal Help if Needed** – Tenant‑rights groups, legal aid clinics, or a private attorney can provide guidance. --- #### Useful Resources | Resource | What It Offers | |----------|----------------| | **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection** | Information on landlord‑tenant laws, dispute resolution. | | **Texas Commission on Human Rights** | Complaint filing for discrimination. | | **Legal Aid of North Texas** | Free legal assistance for qualifying tenants. | | **Texas Tenants’ Rights Guide (PDF)** | Comprehensive guide on rights and responsibilities. | If you have a specific situation (e.g., a dispute over a security deposit, a notice of eviction, or a maintenance issue), let me know and I can give more tailored advice or help draft a letter to your landlord.
